chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn Amer, from Ma'la ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Bastam ibn Marah, from Ishaq ibn Hisan, from Al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Al-Asbagh ibn al-Nubatah said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered us to travel to Madaen from Kufa, so we set out on Sunday. Amr ibn Harith and seven others stayed behind and went to a place in Hira called Al-Khoranq, saying, 'We will amuse ourselves here, and when it is Wednesday, we will leave and catch up with Ali (peace be upon him) before he leads the Friday prayer.'

While they were eating lunch, a lizard emerged before them. They hunted it, and Amr ibn Harith took it, raised his palm, and said, 'Pledge allegiance to this Commander of the Faithful.' The seven pledged allegiance to it, and Amr was the eighth.

They departed on Wednesday night and arrived in Madaen on Friday while the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was delivering the sermon. They did not separate from one another and remained together until they arrived at the door of the mosque. When they entered, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) looked at them.
He said, 'O people! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) disclosed to me one thousand narrations, each containing one thousand gates, and for each gate one thousand keys.'
And I heard God, may His Majesty be Exalted, say: 'One day We shall call every group with their Imam...'
And I swear to you by God that on the Day of Resurrection, eight people will be resurrected with their leader, who will be a lizard. If I wished, I could name them for you.
He said, 'I saw Amr ibn Harith fall down as a date palm branch falls, from shame and reproach.'

key_terms.السَّعْفَةُ: Date palm branch (used as a simile for falling)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمَعَ: Friday (specifically referring to the Friday prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Amr ibn Harith and the lizard in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Al-Khisal* illustrates the concept of *al-Imam al-Mufrad* (the singular leader) through a literal yet profound example, where Amr ibn Harith and his companions pledged allegiance to a lizard during a moment of leisure. Imam Ali (as) uses this incident to demonstrate that one's spiritual status in the Hereafter is determined by their chosen 'imam,' whether divine or mundane, fulfilling the Quranic promise that every group will be called with their imam. The story highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the continuity of leadership and the weight of personal choice in defining one's ultimate destiny.
